node_fragments.note: The schematic two-complementiser-layer configuration: S-double-bar dominates C2 and S-bar; S-bar dominates C1 and S.

no_book_tree: Further Exercises 1–9: no complete phrase-marker answer key is printed in the supplied chapter.
book_flags: Wh-clauses use S-double-bar → C2 + S-bar and S-bar → C1 + S. C2 contains the fronted wh-expression; C1 is the lower complementiser position.
All clause-initial wh-expressions are represented in C2. The chapter assumes C1 auxiliary-fronting in every non-echo main wh-question, including wh-subject questions.
Wh-fronting leaves a gap of the corresponding category; the wh-phrase category in C2 need not be labelled, but the gap category must be represented.
Subordinate wh-interrogatives have an empty C1; auxiliary-fronting occurs only in main wh-questions.
Relative clauses are wh-clauses. Restrictive relatives are sisters of NOM; non-restrictive relatives are sisters of NP. Noun-complement clauses are sisters of N and have no gap.
In relative clauses, the book adopts that as an alternative relative form in C2, not as a C1 complementiser.
The in-text figures [39], [59], and [60] use triangles for internal relative-clause structure; their wh-gap information is retained as metadata rather than expanded inside the triangle.
Movement arrows and dotted movement lines are not part of the phrase marker; they are kept separately in movement metadata where useful.

exercise_1.answer_type: Form the corresponding main wh-question; wh-subject questions retain the subject position in surface order.

exercise_2.answer_type: Embed the supplied finite relative clause in the noun phrase; use the full wh-phrase when the gap is a complement of a preposition.

items.answer: Both relative clauses must be restrictive

review_notes: The schematic [10] is stored as a node fragment rather than a complete sentence tree.
For [39], [59], and [60], the source figure intentionally triangles the internal relative clause; the wh-gap category is described in metadata, not expanded in the printed tree.
In Discussion 3(a), the book gives AP as the usual gap category for how, but explicitly notes a PP alternative; both are recorded.
Exercise 1 and Exercise 2 are represented by concise answer-type notes rather than reproducing the book’s full answer wording; no unprinted phrase markers have been invented.
Further Exercises have no complete tree/ACA answer key in this chapter and are excluded from gold trees.

trees.sentence: What is Vince taking to Athens

trees.sentence: the dogs which have rabies

trees.sentence: the dogs which have rabies
trees.note: Non-restrictive relative clause modifies the complete NP; the printed S-double-bar is triangular. The wh-subject gap is not expanded.

trees.sentence: Which books are you giving to Bill

trees.note: The whole PP to whom is fronted, leaving a PP gap.

trees.note: The usual answer is AP (well/good); the book also allows a PP gap.
